title: Executive Advocate Intake, Handoff, and Roadmap Pledge
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a repeatable process and artifacts that let an internal Executive Advocate intake high-touch customer requests, translate them into prioritized roadmap pledges (tiered commitments), and handoff to engineering and solutions teams with clear acceptance criteria and SLAs. This ticket defines the intake form, routing matrix, pledge tiers (what we commit to deliver, timeline, and risk), and the required handoff package for execution and post-delivery reporting.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form prototype (Confluence + short form) capturing customer ask, business impact, exec sponsor, risk, and desired timeline
Routing matrix mapping request signal (escalation channel, ARR, strategic indicator) to routing path (PM triage, Solutions Eng, Dedicated/Private ops) and SLA for a first response
Three pledge tiers defined (Pledge-A: timeboxed minimal deliverable; Pledge-B: scoped enhancement; Pledge-C: multi-cycle initiative) with standardized timeline windows and required resources
Handoff package template (PRD checklist) that engineering needs to start planning: goals, success metrics, non-goals, data access, security needs, and rollout constraints
Stakeholder RACI for Executive Advocate, PM, Solutions Eng, Engineering Lead, Customer Success established
Pilot with 3 active top-account escalations completed and post-pilot retro recorded
decisions: Use Executive Advocate role as the primary qualifier for ‘roadmap pledge’ eligibility rather than ARR-only threshold (decision made 2025-02-20)
Adopt three pledge tiers to avoid ad-hoc promises: Pledge-A (6-8 weeks), Pledge-B (1-2 quarters), Pledge-C (multi-quarter roadmap initiative)
Routing will prefer Dedicated/Private ops engineers for infra-sensitive asks; hosted-api product changes routed to core PM and runtime team
Commit to a single canonical handoff template (Confluence page) and require an initial engineering-readiness review within 7 business days of pledge acceptance
tradeoffs: Tighter pledge windows increase predictability but may force lower scope; we trade scope for delivery certainty
Requiring Executive Advocate sign-off reduces false positives but adds a gating human step that may slow response to truly urgent technical incidents
Tiered pledges create clarity but may be perceived by some accounts as arbitrary categorization; mitigation: transparent rubric and case reviews
comments: 2025-02-18 - Maya Chen: Kickoff with Customer Success and GTM. Agreed to pilot with three executive-advocate-identified accounts in Q2.
